dimensions.name: Requirements clarification
dimensions.description: Clarifies sync semantics, offline behavior, versions, conflict policy, and durability expectations.

levels.1: Restates the prompt without defining what counts as a synced file.
levels.2: Lists upload and download but omits offline edits, versions, or conflicts.
levels.3: Separates functional and non-functional requirements and states assumptions about sharing, devices, and file sizes.
levels.4: Also prioritizes requirements, defines the durability boundary, and explains how conflict and retention policies affect user trust.

dimensions.name: Back-of-envelope estimation
dimensions.description: Derives metadata QPS, block traffic, storage growth, and peak load from the stated scale.

levels.1: Repeats the numbers without deriving anything.
levels.2: Computes average commit or read rates but ignores block traffic, storage, or peaks.
levels.3: Estimates average and peak metadata QPS, block throughput, and storage growth.
levels.4: Also estimates dedupe savings, cache working sets, large-file upload time, and the capacity needed for version retention.

dimensions.name: API and data model
dimensions.description: Defines metadata and block APIs plus file, version, block, and cursor models.

levels.1: No clear API or data model.
levels.2: Has upload/download endpoints but omits versions, blocks, or change cursors.
levels.3: Defines metadata and block operations, immutable versions, content hashes, and a per-namespace change log.
levels.4: Also explains parent-version checks, idempotent commit, snapshot fallback, and how block references stay consistent.

dimensions.name: High-level architecture
dimensions.description: Separates metadata, block storage, notification, and garbage collection.

levels.1: A single service with no separation of metadata and content.
levels.2: Names components but does not show an upload or delta-sync flow.
levels.3: Shows metadata storage, object storage, notification fan-out, and garbage collection with clear responsibilities.
levels.4: Also explains why the boundary exists, how components scale, and how notifications stay advisory while the cursor remains authoritative.

dimensions.name: Deep dives
dimensions.description: Explains commit durability, delta sync, and conflict resolution with retries and edge cases.

levels.1: No deep dive beyond the API.
levels.2: Covers upload or sync but leaves conflicts and crash recovery vague.
levels.3: Covers upload commit, cursor-based catch-up, and a conflict policy with enough detail to implement.
levels.4: Also handles lost responses, idempotent retries, cursor reset, orphan cleanup, and why the chosen conflict policy never loses data.

dimensions.name: Trade-offs
dimensions.description: Compares chunking, dedupe placement, consistency, push vs poll, and retention.

levels.2: Names one trade-off without connecting it to the design.
levels.3: Compares meaningful options such as fixed vs content-defined chunks, client vs server dedupe, or push vs poll.
levels.4: Also explains when each option would be wrong and how measurements would drive a revisit.

dimensions.name: Communication and failure handling
dimensions.description: Presents a clear design with failure modes, garbage collection, and monitoring.

levels.2: Understandable but omits several failure or cleanup paths.
levels.3: Explains the flow clearly and covers partial uploads, notification outages, cursor resets, and monitoring.
levels.4: Also covers storage corruption, ref-count reconciliation, snapshot recovery, and a concise summary of the key invariants.
